name: The Bereans
charge: Receiving the word with all readiness of mind, and searching the scriptures daily, whether those things were so
summary: Driven from Thessalonica by a mob, Paul and Silas came to Berea and found a synagogue that did two things at once: welcomed the message and checked it against the scriptures every day. Luke calls them more noble than the Thessalonians for it. Many of them believed, including honourable Greek women and men.
offense: These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so. They did not believe Paul because he was Paul; they believed the scriptures, and found him in them.
judgment: Therefore many of them believed; also of honourable women which were Greeks, and of men, not a few. When the Thessalonian Jews came to stir up the city, the brethren sent Paul away, and Silas and Timotheus abode there still. Search the scriptures, Christ had said; the Bereans are the one church named for having done it, and the church was theirs.

entries.commentary: At the pool called Bethesda an angel troubled the water at a certain season, and whosoever first stepped in was made whole. A man had been there thirty and eight years and had no man to put him in. Wilt thou be made whole? Rise, take up thy bed, and walk. He did not have to wait for the water at all, and immediately he was made whole. And on the same day was the sabbath.
The first thing said to a man healed after thirty-eight years is that it is not lawful for him to carry his bed. Not one word about the healing.
Behold, thou art made whole: sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee. The healing came with a charge, and that charge is the keeping of the commandments.

The Jews persecuted him, and sought to slay him, because he had done these things on the sabbath day. He had broken no sabbath. He answers them elsewhere out of their own practice: they circumcise on the sabbath so that the law of Moses be not broken, and a man made every whit whole is greater than that.

My Father worketh hitherto, and I work. They sought the more to kill him, because he said also that God was his Father, making himself equal with God. That attitude toward a just man was written down long before.

The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father do. As the Father raiseth up the dead, and quickeneth them; even so the Son quickeneth whom he will. To quicken is to make alive, and it covers both the raising of the dead and the making alive of men dead in their sins.

The Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son, which is why men stand before the judgment seat of Christ. He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life, and shall not come into condemnation.

The hour is coming, and now is, when the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God: and they that hear shall live. That happened before their eyes with Lazarus, and it reaches forward to the last judgment. All that are in the graves shall hear his voice, and shall come forth; they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life; and they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of damnation.

I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me. Ye sent unto John, and he bare witness unto the truth. He was a burning and a shining light, and ye were willing for a season to rejoice in his light. But I have greater witness than that of John: the works which the Father hath given me to finish bear witness of me.

Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me. They could not match the prophecies to the life being lived in front of them. He had to open the scriptures himself, from Moses through all the prophets, to shew what they said of him.

I am come in my Father's name, and ye receive me not: if another shall come in his own name, him ye will receive. Do not think that I will accuse you to the Father: there is one that accuseth you, even Moses, in whom ye trust. For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me: for he wrote of me. If ye believe not his writings, how shall ye believe my words? A man who will not take what Moses wrote will not take Christ either.
The Most High told Isaiah to take a great roll and write in it with a man's pen concerning Maher-shalal-hash-baz, meaning quick to the plunder, swift to the spoil.

Isaiah took faithful witnesses to record, Uriah the priest and Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah, then went to the prophetess, who conceived and bare a son. The Most High said to call his name Maher-shalal-hash-baz, for before the child shall have knowledge to cry, "My father, and my mother," the riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria shall be taken away before the king of Assyria. This ties to [Isaiah 7:16](/bible/isaiah/7#v16), "before the child shall know to refuse evil and choose the good"; both point to the fall of the lands of Rezin and Pekah.

Because the people refuse the waters of Shiloah that go softly and rejoice in Rezin and Remaliah's son, the Most High brings upon them the waters of the river strong and many, the king of Assyria and all his glory, rising over all his channels and banks. He shall pass through Judah and overflow, reaching even to the neck, and the stretching out of his wings shall fill the breadth of the land, O Immanuel, which means God with us.

"Associate yourselves, O ye people, and ye shall be broken in pieces." Though the far countries gird themselves, they shall be broken; take counsel together and it shall come to nought, speak the word and it shall not stand, for God is with us. If the counsel is from man it will fall, but if it is from the Most High it cannot be overthrown, and men would only end up fighting against God. -

The Most High spoke with a strong hand, instructing Isaiah not to walk in the way of this people, and not to say "a confederacy" to all them to whom this people says a confederacy, nor to fear their fear. "Sanctify the LORD of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread."

He shall be for a sanctuary, but also a stone of stumbling and a rock of offence to both the houses of Israel, and a gin and snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem. He is a sanctuary for his people, a little sanctuary in the places where they are scattered, but a stone of stumbling to those who reject him. The word became a snare upon the leadership because the understanding is given precept upon precept, in another tongue, so that those without it stumble and fall. -
Many among them shall stumble, fall, be broken, snared, and taken.

"Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples." Knowing the law is knowing what the mark truly is, instead of thinking of a microchip and being snared and taken by every wind, like the trees moved with the wind.

"I will wait upon the LORD, that hideth his face from the house of Jacob, and I will look for him." Behold, Isaiah and the children the Most High gave him are for signs and wonders in Israel, from the Lord of hosts which dwelleth in mount Zion.

When they say to seek unto them that have familiar spirits, and wizards that peep and mutter, the answer is: should not a people seek unto their God? For the living to the dead? "To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them." Christians say Jesus is the word and go to [John 17:17](/bible/john/17#v17), "thy word is truth," but the word spoken of is the law; no law means no light, which is why there is no light in christianity. -

They shall pass through it hardly bestead and hungry, fret themselves, and curse their king and their God, looking upward and to the earth. They shall behold trouble and darkness, dimness of anguish, and be driven to darkness.

verses.text: And the brethren immediately sent away Paul and Silas by night unto Berea: who coming thither went into the synagogue of the Jews.
These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.
Therefore many of them believed; also of honourable women which were Greeks, and of men, not a few.
But when the Jews of Thessalonica had knowledge that the word of God was preached of Paul at Berea, they came thither also, and stirred up the people.
And then immediately the brethren sent away Paul to go as it were to the sea: but Silas and Timotheus abode there still.
Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me.
To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them.
O how love I thy law! it is my meditation all the day.
Thou through thy commandments hast made me wiser than mine enemies: for they are ever with me.
I have more understanding than all my teachers: for thy testimonies are my meditation.
I understand more than the ancients, because I keep thy precepts.
But continue thou in the things which thou hast learned and hast been assured of, knowing of whom thou hast learned them;
And that from a child thou hast known the holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus.
All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness:
That the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works.
